== plan ==
1  install what this project is missing
   satisfied=false delegated=false
   why |
     
   describe |
     This package provides dharness's project lint rules.
     
         npm install --save-dev dharness-eslint-plugin
2  write the files dharness owns
   satisfied=false delegated=false
   why |
     
   describe |
     The gate, the architecture and the rule thresholds live in .dharness/, which is
     committed. The project's own files only ever gain one line pointing at them.
3  point .fallowrc.json at the file dharness owns
   satisfied=false delegated=false
   why |
     
   describe |
     fallow composes with `extends`, so the architecture arrives by reference.
     Add this line to .fallowrc.json:
     
         "extends": ["../.dharness/fallow.jsonc"]
4  resolve the two architectures this project declares
   satisfied=true delegated=true
   why |
     .fallowrc.json declares its own `boundaries`, and fallow's `extends` replaces that key
     rather than merging it — the project's block replaces the one dharness owns
     entirely, without an error. Only one architecture is being enforced, and the
     configuration does not say which.
   describe |
     Move the zones and rules from .fallowrc.json into .dharness/fallow.jsonc, or delete the block dharness
     owns and keep the project's. Either is a valid answer; having both is not,
     because only one of them runs and the file gives no sign of which.
5  point lefthook.yml at the file dharness owns
   satisfied=true delegated=false
   why |
     
   describe |
     lefthook composes with `extends`, so the gate arrives by reference.
     Add this line to lefthook.yml:
     
         extends:
           - .dharness/lefthook.yml
6  fix the lint config react-doctor silently drops
   satisfied=true delegated=true
   why |
     .eslintrc.json does not parse. react-doctor adopts this file and runs the rules in it,
     so a broken one drops them all — measured: the same rules that failed the gate
     with exit 1 report nothing and it exits 0, naming the file nowhere, not even
     under --verbose. Repairing it means knowing what it was meant to say.
   describe |
     Make .eslintrc.json parse, or delete it. Either answer is fine; a file that is present
     and unreadable is not, because the gate cannot tell you which rules it stopped
     running.
7  give the agent fallow's own tools
   satisfied=false delegated=false
   why |
     
   describe |
     fallow ships an MCP server with the analysis an agent would otherwise ask a
     wrapper to invent: boundaries, traces, impact, health.
8  wire the gate into git
   satisfied=false delegated=true
   why |
     nothing answers: there is no lefthook config, no .husky/ and no lefthook
     binary. Choosing a hook manager is a decision this project has not made, and
     not a default dharness gets to pick.
   describe |
     Choose a hook manager and wire it to run the gate:
     
         dharness check
     
     lefthook writes its own git hook once configured and installed; husky keeps
     a shell script that needs one appended line. Either way, the step is
     satisfied once "dharness check" runs on commit.
9  install react-doctor's agent skill
   satisfied=false delegated=true
   why |
     its only non-interactive form installs five things: skills for every agent it
     detects, a package script, a git hook that competes with this gate, and a CI
     workflow. There is no flag to ask for the skill alone.
   describe |
         npx --yes react-doctor@latest install
     
     Choose the skill and decline the rest.
10  decide this project's architecture
   satisfied=false delegated=true
   why |
     architecture boundaries say what the code is meant to be, and no tool can
     read intent off a tree. Do the analysis and write the result — nothing else
     needs to change.
   describe |
     ### What the framework already documents
     
     - Next.js documents four top-level folders: app/ (App Router) or pages/ (Pages Router) for routing, public/ for static assets served as-is, and an optional src/ that wraps the rest. Routes are a delivery shell around the domain, not domain modules themselves.
       (https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/project-structure — Next.js's own documented top-level project structure)
     - Beyond routing, Next.js takes no position on how the rest of the source is organized — read the real seams off this tree rather than assuming a components/ or lib/ convention.
       (https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/project-structure: "Next.js is unopinionated about how you organize and colocate your project files," and its own components/lib example folders "have no special framework significance.")
     
     Confirm or correct this against the tree. It names structure, not
     zones — those are still read from the code and the person who wrote it,
     never from this list.
     
     ### What to find out
     
     1. Read the source layout. What are the real seams: features, layers, a
        delivery shell around a domain, a monorepo of packages that repeat the same
        internal shape?
     2. Follow the imports that cross those seams today. A boundary that half the
        codebase already violates is a wish, not an architecture — say so rather
        than declaring it and drowning the gate.
     3. Decide whether one of the presets already describes this project:
        `bulletproof`, `layered`, `hexagonal` or `feature-sliced`. A preset is one
        line and expands into zones and rules on its own.
     4. If none fits, declare zones by glob. `autoDiscover` isolates every feature
        under a directory without listing them; `root` scopes a zone to one package
        of a monorepo, which is how several packages share an internal layout
        without sharing zones.
     5. Ask the person you are working with whatever the code cannot answer. This
        is a decision about intent, and they hold it.
     
     ### Where to write it
     
         .dharness/fallow.jsonc
     
     That file is already referenced from this project's fallow configuration, so
     writing the `boundaries` block there is the whole change.
     
     ### How to check the result
     
         npx --yes fallow@latest list --boundaries
     
     It prints every zone with the number of files it matched and the rules already
     expanded, and warns when a zone matched nothing — which is what a glob that
     does not fit this tree looks like. A zone with zero files is a mistake, not a
     style choice.
     
         npx --yes fallow@latest dead-code --boundary-violations
     
     Then read what the declaration costs today. Violations that already exist are
     reported but do not block: the gate fails only on the ones a change
     introduces, so an architecture can be declared on a codebase that does not
     yet obey it. Type-only imports do count as crossings, and imports of
     external packages do not.
     
     ### The one rule dharness will not choose for you
     
     When a module splits into role files — `*.types.ts`, `*.helpers.ts` and the
     rest — does this project publish it through an `index.ts`, or does it import
     the concrete files?
     
     Both are architectures, not one right answer. A project can have good
     reasons to ban barrel files outright, and one that does cannot satisfy a rule
     demanding the file it deleted — every split module would report forever.
     
     So `folder-ownership` ships **off**. The other five rules are guardrails on
     generated code and stay on; this one is the only one that takes a side.
     
     If this project does publish through barrels, turn it on in frontend/doctor.config.json:
     
         "rules": {
           "dharness/folder-ownership": "error"
         }
     
     A severity written there survives every later run: dharness fills in only the
     rules a project has not answered for itself.
     

== tree ==
.dharness/.gitignore
---
# dharness — this directory is written by dharness.
# Everything here is machine-local unless it is named below, so transient files
# (incremental reports, caches) never show up in git.
*
!.gitignore
!lefthook.yml
!fallow.jsonc
!rules.json
!evidence.json
!eslint.config.js
---
.dharness/eslint.config.js
---
// dharness writes this file. It exports a factory rather than a config
// array because the packages it names are installed beside the project's
// package.json, and a bare specifier resolves from the file that writes it
// — which, in a split layout, is not this directory.
export default function dharnessLayer({ plugin }) {
  return [
    {
      plugins: { dharness: plugin },
      rules: {
        "dharness/folder-ownership": "off",
        "dharness/max-file-lines": "error",
        "dharness/pure-index-barrel": "error",
        "dharness/require-jsdoc": "error",
        "dharness/require-variable-jsdoc": "error",
        "dharness/role-file-shape": "error",
      },
    },
  ];
}
---
.dharness/fallow.jsonc
---
{
  // dharness:presets begin — rewritten by `dharness sync`; edits here are lost.
  // wails: wails.json declares no "wailsjsdir", so the default Wails itself falls back to (frontend/) applies
  "ignorePatterns": ["wailsjs/**"],
  // generic: dharness compares structure rather than text (mode "semantic"), reports a clone group only from 3 occurrences, and caps duplication at 3%. fallow's own defaults are mild, 2 and no limit, so all three are departures rather than restatements: structural matching still finds the copy-paste that has since diverged, two occurrences is usually coincidence where three is a pattern, and the ceiling is borrowed from the SonarQube gate this toolchain already answers to — different algorithms, so they corroborate rather than repeat each other
  "duplicates": {"minOccurrences":3,"mode":"semantic","threshold":3},
  // dharness:presets end

  // dharness writes this file; the architecture below is decided by analysis,
  // not by detection. Declare `boundaries` here rather than in the project's
  // own fallow config: `extends` replaces this key, it does not merge it.
  //
  // See `dharness sync`.
}
---
.dharness/lefthook.yml
---
pre-commit:
  commands:
    dharness:
      run: dharness check
      root: frontend/
---
.dharness/rules.json
---
{
  "schema": "dharness.rules/v1",
  "maxFileLines": 500,
  "roleSuffixes": [
    ".types.ts",
    ".constants.ts",
    ".helpers.ts",
    ".schema.ts"
  ]
}
